quarterly_data.quarter: Tempus AI press release: Tempus Launches Effort to Build the Largest Multimodal (09-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Tempus announced an initiative to build a research platform containing 100,000 whole genomes linked to longitudinal clinical information over the next several years, which the company calls the first de-identified multimodal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) dataset built around disease populations and patient outcomes, optimized for AI-driven research (company claim); once complete, Tempus plans to expand the effort with the goal of reaching one million genomes. The WGS data will be integrated into Tempus' existing de-identified multimodal data environment and accessed through Tempus Lens, where researchers and model developers can build and validate AI models without moving datasets, with a computational system for pre-training and post-training workflows. Development is already underway; the initial dataset is available through Tempus' Early Adopter Program, additional members will be onboarded in waves, and general availability is planned for mid-2027. CEO Eric Lefkofsky: adding whole genome data linked to longitudinal outcomes 'makes that platform even more powerful and gives researchers a richer foundation to build AI models.'
quarterly_data.figure: 100,000 whole genomes over the next several years; long-term goal of one million genomes; general availability planned for mid-2027
